elements.text: Pilot's pattern of poor decision-making leading to initial launch, continued flight in fog/above clouds, and descent near clouds
FAA policy not requiring a medical certificate for commercial balloon pilots
No preimpact structural or system failures in the balloon
Pilot's failure to obtain updated weather information despite available data indicating deteriorating conditions
Pilot's decision to launch when he should have cancelled
Pilot's failure to land the balloon despite suitable opportunities in visual conditions
Pilot's decision to climb above the clouds
Pilot's decision to land in reduced visibility conditions
Balloon impacting power lines obscured by low clouds/fog
Support cables striking power lines causing separation of basket and release of fuel
Pilot not under influence of alcohol or illicit drugs
Pilot's high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, chronic back pain, and fibromyalgia did not affect performance
Prescribed medications for high blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, and depression did not affect performance
Depression, ADHD, and combined effects of multiple CNS-impairing drugs likely affected pilot's ability to make safe decisions
FAA exemption from medical certification eliminated opportunity for medical examiner to identify impairing conditions/medications
FAA exemption eliminated opportunity for FAA awareness of pilot's history of drug/alcohol offenses
FAA's primary oversight method (sampling at festivals) does not effectively target high-risk operations
